P001.note: Comments on the introductory article on economic and social rights of the human being as a member of society (French proposal, Egyptian 'within the limits of their possibilities'), the article that became UDHR 22.

P002.note: Cuba on the place of article 1 (moving it to the preamble or a separate chapter 'Essential Principles').

P003.note: On whether the Human Rights Committee's decisions need a majority of members present or voting (Committee procedure/voting), not the composition of the Committee.

P004.note: Cassin on States nominating candidates to the panel for the Committee, in the debate on nominations.

P005.note: Baroody on the three-Power resolution and Afghan amendments setting a working party and deadline for the final text of article 1 (self-determination); procedural but tied to the article's text (borderline).

P006.note: Yu explains his vote on paragraphs 8-9 and the last paragraph of the education article (same 'Article 1' education text whose final paragraph is the organisation-and-resources clause); fairly confident from parallel items.

P007.note: UK asks that the report note its preferred text of draft article 2 (the limitations/duties article), just adopted.

P008.note: Chang on placing article 2 (limitations/duties) at the end of the Declaration and on its reconsideration.

P009.note: Egypt on the procedure of acceptance and which States may sign the Covenant (with a remark on entry into force).

P010.note: Santa Cruz on the UNESCO education texts, minorities' cultural development and opposing the parents' choice clause of UDHR 26(3) in the Covenant's education article.

P011.note: Egypt on the general obligations article for economic, social and cultural rights (French proposal, 'by legislative or other methods').

P012.note: US opposes a motion for division of the inter-State communications text; voting in parts on the article (context only).

P013.note: Panama on deciding first whether article 1 stays or moves to the preamble (its place).

P014.note: General debate on whether a federal clause should be included at all (the federal clause question, which the rules treat as general); borderline since art. 50 is the outcome of that debate.

P015.note: Chile on to whom the Committee's report in an inter-State case is sent (delete 'to the States concerned').

P016.note: USSR asks for its amendment to the education article to be put to the vote; the Chairman rules voting has begun.

P017.note: Uruguay on the UNESCO education proposal, free education and parents' rights.

P018.note: CSW on moving the paragraph on special protection of mothers and children (the later UDHR 25(2)) into another article; about that paragraph.

P020.note: Cassin on the Committee's report in inter-State cases where a friendly settlement is reached.

P021.note: Short reply in the freedom of movement debate that non-discrimination falls under equality before the law; low confidence about its link to the article.

P022.note: Malik on grouping fundamental rights and including physical integrity in the right-to-life article (draft art. 4).

P023.note: Decision to include a general umbrella article on economic, social and cultural rights (the general obligations article).

P024.note: Procedural suggestion on the UK previous question whether draft article 23 should be included; correct only if draft art. 23 is the standard-of-living article (cannot verify).

P025.note: UK on the Egyptian amendment about transmitting State reports to the Secretary-General and specialized agencies.

P026.note: Chile asks the US to resubmit its text as an amendment to the original draft article 20 (right to work) in the order of votes.

P028.note: Cassin asks the report to mention deletion of the article barring the Committee from matters covered by special UN/specialized agency procedures.

P029.note: UK on the non-judicial character of the Committee in the debate on members' qualifications (texts A and B).

P030.note: USSR on whether to deal now with the UK proposal for a reservations article (reservations question/order of business), not the substance of the general obligations article.

P031.note: Greece wants States' obligations for ESC rights stated in an opening general article.

P032.note: Egypt on the Chilean suggestion of a waiting period in the amendments article (art. 73).

P033.note: Denmark withdraws its proposal (E/CN.4/547) in the right-to-work debate.

P034.note: USSR agrees to defer deciding where (which covenant) the self-determination article goes; about its place.

P035.note: Chile and Uruguay will not press a vote at second reading but enter reservations in the report; cannot tell from the item which article, judged in context.

P036.note: Lebanon accepts the voting procedure on the education article and reserves its amendment on compulsory education.

P037.note: USSR on the order of votes on adjourning paragraphs 2 and 3 of the UK text of the derogation article.

P038.note: USSR on voting new proposals before the motion to delete paragraph 2 of the saving-clause article.

P039.note: Lebanon on the Belgian wording replacing 'with a view to a friendly settlement' in the inter-State procedure.

P040.note: Belgium on defining 'peoples' under the agenda item on recommendations for respect of self-determination (the general question), not the covenant article.

P041.note: Italy asks for a suspension to redraft the article on reporting in stages (draft art. 18) after debate on ECOSOC's role.

P042.note: UK suggests deferring purely drafting changes to the US amendment of the general obligations article.

P043.note: Belgium corrects the French text of paragraph 2 of the inter-State complaint article (notifying the Secretary-General and the other State).

P044.note: Ukraine asks for a vote on its amendment opening the Covenant for signature to any State.

P045.note: US presents its additional article on reporting under the civil and political covenant.

P046.note: Request for a vote in parts and roll-call on Malik's amendment to the marriage/family article.

P047.note: AFL on draft article 4 (exceptions/derogations), favouring a general limitative clause with non-derogable rights and notification.

P048.note: India on its amendment on the content of the Committee's report in inter-State cases.

P049.note: Denmark withdraws its amendment to the Yugoslav text in the trade union rights debate.

P050.note: Australia explains its abstention on the ESC covenant's federal-States article (draft art. 27).

P051.note: Sweden on the length and content of the education provision.

P052.note: Roosevelt on the US amendment turning paragraph 4 of article 19 into the first general obligations article (also rejects the USSR amendment to art. 20).

P053.note: India questions the special provisions on the method of electing Committee members.

P054.note: UK explains its vote on the article on the Committee's secretariat, bringing its administration under the Secretary-General.

P055.note: Cassin on including persons who held high judicial office among Committee members (qualifications).

P056.note: Uruguay on ensuring the Committee meets whenever a complaint is presented.

P058.note: Cassin on his general obligations text and working out a joint text with Yugoslavia and the US.

P059.note: Philippines notes the CSW agreed to the text of the work article being voted (women working under the same conditions as men).

P060.note: Chang proposes mentioning public examinations for admission to public office (equal access to public service).

P061.note: USSR opposes a sub-committee and asks for its amendment to the slavery article to be voted first.

P062.note: Greece: the Committee's report in inter-State cases should go to the Secretary-General for publication.

P063.note: Denmark on the election of Committee members by the ICJ.

P064.note: USSR opposes wording referring to the categories of States in the signature article and asks a separate vote on paragraph 2 of new article 29 ter (likely authentic texts/certified copies); moderate confidence.

P066.note: Chang on the paragraphs of the fair trial/presumption of innocence/non-retroactivity article.

P067.note: UK explains its vote against the resolution setting up the working party on the text of article 1 (self-determination); procedural but tied to the article (borderline).

P068.note: On which parties 'having an interest' in a case may take part before the Committee (inter-State procedure), not the Committee's officers and rules.

P069.note: Chile clarifies its position on the joint Ecuador-Peru-Chile amendment to the self-determination article.

P070.note: UK on how the report summarises the debate on the equality before the law article.

P071.note: Pakistan's general position on including a federal clause (the federal clause question); borderline since a draft federal clause article was under discussion.

P072.note: Haiti on the Yugoslav proposal on application to Non-Self-Governing Territories (later UDHR 2, second paragraph).

P073.note: Belgium opposes the Chilean amendment on reporting facts after a friendly settlement in inter-State cases.

P074.note: WHO on the right to health provision.

P075.note: USSR opposes the final 'organization and resources' paragraph of the education article.

P076.note: Lebanon on 'present and voting' in the majority required for election of Committee members (draft art. 6).

P077.note: Chang on the new article on the right to a good social order and its link with duties.

P078.note: France: the juridical personality article concerns total deprivation of legal personality, not stateless persons.

P079.note: France on the US text of the general obligations article (jurisdiction, 'nationals', deleting paragraph (b)).

P082.note: China on keeping the federal clause (draft art. 24) separate from the colonial clause (the federal clause question); borderline.

P085.note: ILO on the draft resolution on minor communal services in connection with the forced labour article's exceptions.

P086.note: Mongolia on treaty participation not implying recognition, in the debate on the 'all States' signature formula.

P089.note: Chile on the arresting authority's duty to bring the detainee before a court without delay (arrest article).
